Wounded in the arm at the Trench, Sa'd bin Mu'adh was nursed in a tent the Prophet pitched in the mosque, until his wound bled profusely and he died there.
On the day of the Trench Umar said he could not pray Asr before sunset; the Prophet made ablution at Buthan and prayed Asr after sunset, then Maghrib.
On the day of the Trench neither Umar nor the Prophet had prayed Asr before sunset; the Prophet made ablution at Buthan and prayed Asr, then Maghrib.
Digging the trench, cold and hungry Emigrants and Ansar pledge lifelong jihad, while the Prophet, carrying earth, asks Allah to forgive and bless them and grant calm and firm feet.
At the Trench the Prophet carries earth until dust covers his chest hair, loudly reciting Abdullah bin Rawaha's verses asking Allah for calm and firm feet against the enemy.
Jabir invites the Prophet and a few others to a young sheep and a Sa of barley, but the Prophet loudly calls the people of the Trench to come.
Emigrants and Ansar dig the trench hungry as the Prophet carries earth and asks Allah's forgiveness for them; Jabir's meal feeds a thousand, and Ibn Umar fights aged fifteen.
The Prophet says Muslims will now attack the clans, not be attacked; Asr is delayed past sunset, Az-Zubair is called his disciple, and Allah alone defeated the clans.
At the Trench the Prophet carried earth, saying without Allah they would not have been guided, fasted or prayed, and asking for calm and firm feet against the enemy.
Carrying earth on the day of the Confederates, the Prophet said that without Allah they would not be guided, give charity or pray, asking tranquillity as the enemy had rebelled.
